# Training recipe

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">All 6 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set optimizer=</code><code class="gp-chip">--set schedule=</code><code class="gp-chip">--set hooks=</code><code class="gp-chip">--set augment=</code><code class="gp-chip">--set recipe=</code><span class="gp-chip">37 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The training recipe is everything around the model: how weights are updated, how the learning
rate moves, what runs around the training loop and how a training sample is perturbed. None of
it changes what the detector computes.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o graspnet-baseline_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list optimizer
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o gsnet_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list optimizer
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o scale-balanced-grasp_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list optimizer
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o economicgrasp_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list optimizer
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o finegrasp_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list optimizer
    ```

=== "HGGD"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e \
        --set optimizer=adamw -o hggd_adamw.yaml
    grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --list optimizer
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#optimizer) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#optimizer) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#optimizer) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#optimizer) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#optimizer) · [HGGD](../methods/hggd.md#optimizer).

<!-- method-options:end -->

`optimizer`, `schedule` and `recipe` take one preset; `hooks` and `augment` take several joined
by `+`, as in `--set hooks=ema+grad-clip`. `--opts` changes single values and wins over a preset:
`--opts optimizer.lr=3e-3 train.epochs=20`.

??? note "What the columns say, and who is left out"

    - **Runs**: out of the methods the option is a swap under, those under which its probe trained on real frames without error. A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: out of the methods under which the swap ran, those under which every comparable loss term ended within the method's tolerance of the component it ships, with nothing rising; a method left out is named with why. Measured on 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.
    - **Schedules** have no level 2: level 2 holds the schedule of the method as shipped fixed (a constant rate; FineGrasp: its own warm-up), so a schedule swap is not compared.
    - [How we measure](../evidence/index.md) defines every word of these columns.

    Who is left out, and why:

    - `encoder-lr-0.1`, runs: seed-based only: it is written for the scene encoder of the seed-based skeleton (`model.backbone`), which HGGD does not have; compose refuses it.
    - `encoder-lr-0.1`, trains like shipped: worse under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, EconomicGrasp; diverging under FineGrasp.
    - `layer-decay`, runs: seed-based only: it is written for the scene encoder of the seed-based skeleton (`model.backbone`), which HGGD does not have; compose refuses it.
    - `schedulefree-adamw`, trains like shipped: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, HGGD: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped.
    - `schedulefree-radam`, trains like shipped: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, HGGD: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped.
    - `schedulefree-sgd`, runs: not GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp (unstable twice in the short probe).
    - `schedulefree-sgd`, trains like shipped: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, HGGD: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped; not compared under GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1.
    - `soap`, runs: not HGGD (not verified: one CUDA illegal memory access on a shared GPU).
    - `timm-adan`, trains like shipped: worse under GSNet, EconomicGrasp, HGGD; diverging under FineGrasp.
    - `timm-lion`, trains like shipped: worse under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, HGGD; diverging under Scale-Balanced-Grasp.
    - `timm-madgrad`, trains like shipped: diverging under GraspNet-baseline; worse under Scale-Balanced-Grasp, FineGrasp.
    - `freeze-encoder`, runs: seed-based only: it is written for the scene encoder of the seed-based skeleton (`model.backbone`), which HGGD does not have; compose refuses it.
    - `freeze-encoder`, trains like shipped: not compared under FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1.
    - `swa`, runs: not GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp (not verified: the probe is shorter than the epoch at which averaging starts).
    - `dropout`, runs: not FineGrasp (fails: the transform order of the composed config is wrong (DepthNormals must run first)).
    - `finetune-encoder`, runs: seed-based only: it is written for the scene encoder of the seed-based skeleton (`model.backbone`), which HGGD does not have; compose refuses it.
    - `ptv3-adamw-onecycle`, runs: seed-based only: it needs `--set backbone=ptv3`, a slot HGGD does not have.

## Choosing

- **The method's own recipe stays** where no preset replaces a part; the composed file lists
  what each preset says must be re-tuned.
- **A pretrained scene encoder:** `--set recipe=finetune-encoder`, or its parts
  `optimizer=encoder-lr-0.1`, `optimizer=layer-decay` and `hooks=freeze-encoder`. They name the
  scene encoder, so they apply to the seed-based methods only.
- **Learning-rate-free and schedule-free optimizers:** `prodigy` wants `lr: 1.0`; each
  `schedulefree-*` preset sets the optimizer, no schedule and its hook together.
- **One weight average per run:** `ema` or `swa`; `evaluation.weights: ema` scores the average.
- **Point augmentation moves points**, which a method that reads images cannot follow; `dropout`
  removes points and moves none.

## Details

??? note "Where the recipe lives in a config"

    | Config key | Registry | What it decides | When it runs |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `optimizer` | `OPTIMIZERS` | how gradients become weight updates | once per `train.accumulate` batches |
    | `scheduler` | `SCHEDULERS` | the learning rate over the run | after every optimizer step or every epoch (`train.scheduler_unit`) |
    | `hooks` | `HOOKS` | anything else around the loop: weight averages, freezing, clipping variants | at `before_run`, `before_epoch`, `before_step`, `after_iter`, `after_epoch`, `after_run` |
    | `data.train.dataset.transforms` | `TRANSFORMS` | augmentation of one training sample | in the data-loader workers, per sample |

    Plain options of the loop need no component: `train.amp`, `train.accumulate`,
    `train.grad_clip` with `train.grad_clip_mode`, `train.ema`, `train.sync_bn`. Three
    method-neutral files under `configs/_base_/schedules/` can be inherited without compose:
    `adamw_onecycle_10e.yaml`, `adamw_warmup-cosine_10e.yaml`, `schedulefree-adamw_10e.yaml`.

??? note "Input and output"

    - **Optimizer.** Built from the `optimizer` node; the engine supplies `params` (or what the
      detector's `configure_optimizers` returns) and, where asked, `model`. The bridges return
      the library's own optimizer, so checkpoints hold its state unchanged.
    - **Scheduler.** Built per optimizer; the trainer steps it per optimizer step
      (`train.scheduler_unit: iteration`) or per epoch. The engine fills in the length of the
      run where a schedule needs it. `scheduler: null` is a constant rate.
    - **Hook.** A subclass of `grasppanda.engine.hooks.Hook`; every callback receives the
      training state. Hooks run in ascending `priority` (evaluation is 70, checkpointing 80). A
      weight average installs itself as `state.ema`, which `evaluation.weights: ema` scores.
    - **Transform.** Maps one `PointSample` to one `PointSample`. It may remove or reorder points
      only through `sample.gather(index)`, which carries the labels; move the scene only with the
      object poses; and not move points at all when the sample carries images, as HGGD's does
      (the config check refuses that list). Scaling the scene is not allowed: grasp widths,
      depths and the gripper are in metres.
    - **The config check** tests every key against the constructor of the named class without
      importing the optional libraries; free-form arguments of a library go into `options`. A
      wrong optimizer name is found when the optimizer is built, with the list of valid ones.

??? note "Optimizers and parameter groups"

    ```yaml
    optimizer: {type: AdamW, lr: 1.0e-3, weight_decay: 0.05}                    # torch.optim, by class
    optimizer: {type: TimmOptimizer, name: lamb, lr: 2.0e-3, weight_decay: 0.02}
    optimizer: {type: PytorchOptimizer, name: prodigy, lr: 1.0}
    optimizer: {type: ScheduleFree, name: adamw, lr: 2.5e-3, warmup_steps: 200}
    ```

    - `lr` and `weight_decay` are arguments of the bridge; everything else (`betas`, `eps`,
      `momentum`) goes into `options`. A `lookahead_` prefix wraps any timm optimizer.
    - A schedule-free optimizer needs `scheduler: null` and `ScheduleFreeHook`; its presets set
      all three.

    `ParamGroups` wraps any optimizer with a rate per module and layer-wise decay:

    ```yaml
    optimizer:
      type: ParamGroups
      optimizer: {type: AdamW, lr: 1.0e-3, weight_decay: 0.05}
      lr_multipliers: {backbone: 0.1}      # dotted prefix of the parameter name, or "re:<regex>"
      layer_decay: 0.75                    # null: off
      layer_decay_module: backbone
      layer_decay_depth: 2
      no_decay_1d: true                    # no weight decay on biases and normalisation weights
    ```

    The rate of a parameter is `lr` × the first matching multiplier × `layer_decay ** (L - i)`
    for layer `i` of the `L` layers of `layer_decay_module`, counted in registration order (a
    U-Net's decoder counts as later layers). To train a pretrained encoder, load its weights
    with `runtime.load_from=<checkpoint>` and `runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true`, then use the
    encoder presets.

??? note "Schedules, hooks and augmentation"

    ```yaml
    scheduler: {type: OneCycleLR, max_lr: 1.0e-3, pct_start: 0.05, div_factor: 10.0, cycle_momentum: false}
    scheduler: {type: TimmSchedule, name: cosine, warmup_steps: 0.05, warmup_lr_init: 1.0e-6, lr_min: 1.0e-6}
    hooks:
      - {type: EMAHook, decay: 0.999, warmup: true, interval: 1, buffers: copy}
      - {type: FreezeHook, modules: [backbone], epochs: 2, eval_mode: true}
    evaluation: {weights: ema}
    ```

    - `TimmSchedule.warmup_steps` below 1 is a fraction of the run, from 1 a step count;
      `warmup_lr_init` and `lr_min` are absolute rates.
    - `EMAHook`, `SWAHook` and `train.ema` exclude each other. `EMAHook` warms its decay up and
      copies buffers by default (batch-norm statistics and HGGD's learned anchors stay those of
      the trained model).
    - `FreezeHook` sets `requires_grad` per epoch, so nothing is rebuilt when modules are
      released. `AdaptiveGradClipHook` and `train.grad_clip` exclude each other.
    - `--set augment=dropout+shift+jitter` writes `RandomDropout` before the sampling step and
      `RandomShift` and `RandomJitter` after the base list. Units are metres in the camera frame;
      `RandomJitter` perturbs only the network input.

??? note "Components and their sources"

    `pip install -e ".[optim]"` installs timm, pytorch_optimizer and schedulefree (all
    Apache-2.0); the rest needs nothing beyond the core install.

    | Component | Kind | What it is | Code |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `TimmOptimizer`, `TimmSchedule` | optimizer, schedule | any optimizer or schedule of timm by `name` | bridge to `timm.optim`, `timm.scheduler` |
    | `PytorchOptimizer` | optimizer | any optimizer of pytorch_optimizer by `name` | bridge to `pytorch_optimizer.load_optimizer` |
    | `ScheduleFree`, `ScheduleFreeHook` | optimizer, hook | schedule-free AdamW, RAdam or SGD ([arXiv 2405.15682](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15682)) and the switch between its training point and its average | bridge to `schedulefree` |
    | `ParamGroups` | optimizer | rate per module, layer-wise decay (BEiT, [arXiv 2106.08254](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.08254)), no decay on 1-D parameters | written here |
    | classes of `torch.optim` and `torch.optim.lr_scheduler` | optimizer, schedule | `AdamW`, `SGD`, `OneCycleLR`, `CosineAnnealingLR`, … | PyTorch |
    | `WarmupCosineLR` | schedule | linear warm-up then cosine, in closed form (FineGrasp's schedule) | written here |
    | `EMAHook`, `SWAHook` | hook | weight averages ([arXiv 1703.01780](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.01780), [arXiv 1803.05407](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05407)) | `torch.optim.swa_utils.AveragedModel` |
    | `FreezeHook` | hook | freeze sub-modules for the first epochs (gradual unfreezing, [arXiv 1801.06146](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06146)) | written here |
    | `AdaptiveGradClipHook` | hook | adaptive gradient clipping ([arXiv 2102.06171](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06171)) | bridge to `timm.utils.adaptive_clip_grad` |
    | `RandomJitter`, `RandomDropout`, `RandomShift` | transform | noise on the points, removal of points with their labels, a shift of the scene and the object poses | adapted from [Pointcept](https://github.com/Pointcept/Pointcept) @ 1342eda (MIT) |

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **`OneCycleLR` and momentum.** Its default `cycle_momentum: true` rewrites `betas` or
      `momentum` every step; the presets set `false`. Its peak is `max_lr`: changing
      `optimizer.lr` changes nothing.
    - **Schedule-free and batch norm.** The evaluated weights are an average, but the batch-norm
      statistics were collected at the training point; this toolbox does not re-estimate them.
    - **Short probes and warm-ups.** With `warmup_steps: 200` a 20-iteration probe runs inside
      the warm-up, so its losses fall slowly; that says nothing about a full run.
    - **Per-epoch units and warm-up.** With `train.scheduler_unit: epoch` a warm-up from 0
      spends the first epoch at rate 0; `multistep-warmup` starts at 1e-4.
    - **Lists replace.** `hooks` and `transforms` of a child config replace the inherited list;
      compose writes the base's entries out again, a hand-written child must repeat them (HGGD
      needs its `EpochSignalHook`).
    - **`SWAHook.start_epoch` must be below `train.epochs`**; the run refuses to start otherwise.
      A short probe ends before averaging starts, so such a probe says nothing about fit.
    - **Mixed precision is refused for the ported methods.** When it was tried, the label
      assigner of the seed-based skeleton wrote half-precision values into a single-precision
      tensor, and HGGD's first loss was not finite. `hooks=amp` sets `train.amp: true`, which the
      config check now refuses unless the detector declares `amp_ready = True`; none of the
      shipped detectors does. The preset is the switch for a detector of your own.
    - **A wrong optimizer name passes the config check** and fails when the optimizer is built,
      with the list of valid names.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | Normalisation and activation as config keys | no shared layer builder exists in the stages; a hook that swapped modules after construction would not run at test time. |
    | `RandomScale`, `ElasticDistortion` | grasp widths, depths and the gripper are in metres, and labels attach to rigid object poses. |
    | Chromatic transforms | the scene encoders read no colour; HGGD's image pipeline is not a point transform. |
    | Mix3D scene mixing | works in the collate function, and two scenes' labels would have to be merged. |
    | Sharpness-aware minimisation (SAM) | its `step()` needs a second forward and backward pass. |
    | `ReduceLROnPlateau` | steps on a monitored metric, which the trainer does not hand to schedules; refused by name. |
    | Batch-norm re-estimation after SWA | `update_bn` iterates plain tensors; batches here are `Batch` objects. |
